thread:
maria (support): heads up — INC-7812 from Acme: after last night's global rollout (redwood-3b-v2), they see hallucinations / factual regressions but only for EU traffic. US and APAC fine.

maria (support): sample prompt from Acme (they're hitting via hosted api in eu-west-1):

acme-ops: "Summarize the following bank statement: ..."
Expected: accurate date/amounts.
Observed (EU): wrong amounts, invented merchant names.
Observed (US/APAC): correct.

maria (support): they attached a small repro curl against eu gateway, I reproduced quickly from our eu bastion — can confirm different output compared to us-east via same prompt + seed.

maria (support): repro steps they provided: 
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-3b-v2","prompt":"<their prompt>","max_tokens":200,"temperature":0.0}'
2) compare outputs for region-specific endpoint (eu vs us)

chen (eng-ml): any chance it's model sharding / kv cache mismatch on MIG partitions? we've seen rare token alignment bugs when batcher selection differs.

david (eng-runtime): hmm — rollout included a kernel tweak and a new quantization fallback path for smaller GPU partitions (MIG). Could be related. I will check the runtime logs for the eu clusters that handled Acme traffic.

olivia (sre): logs from eu-mig-cluster-2 show repeated warnings during inference: 
```
[2026-03-14T02:13:47Z] warn: kernel_selector: selected fallback kernel: matmul_v2_fallback
[2026-03-14T02:13:48Z] warn: kv_cache: partial_eviction triggered on partition 1
[2026-03-14T02:13:48Z] info: batcher: continuous_batcher applied batch_size=1 due to latency SLO
```

olivia (sre): the same model on eu-nonmig nodes doesn't show the warnings.

david (eng-runtime): that batch_size=1 fallback is suspicious — it can change attention alignment ordering in the kernel. If MIG partitions have a different geom or quant path, outputs could diverge even with same seed/temperature.

chen (eng-ml): can we reproduce with an in-cluster run? I can push a small test job pinned to the eu-mig pool. Need the request payload and the exact model hash.

maria (support): provided model hash: sha256:4a7f...; they say it was identical across regions after rollout. Ticket TKT-981 references the canary -> global transition at 2026-03-13 23:00 UTC.

david (eng-runtime): deploying a debug job now pinned to the eu-mig partition. will run the exact prompt with deterministic flags (temperature=0, seed=42, deterministic=true) across eu-mig, eu-nonmig, and us-east nodes.

deploy-bot: started job dbg-1771008642-eu-mig (node: eu-mig-02, image: redwood-runtime:2026-03-13-2145)

(15m later)

david (eng-runtime): results.
- eu-mig (eu-mig-02): output A (hallucinated amounts)
- eu-nonmig (eu-non-03): output B (correct)
- us-east (us-gpu-12): output B (correct)

chen (eng-ml): can you paste the token-level logits diff? particularly at attention weights for token 12-16 where the numbers are produced.

olivia (sre): attaching kernel and driver versions from eu-mig-02: 
```
NVIDIA-SMI 530.41.03
CUDA Version: 12.1
Driver Version: 530.41.03
MIG Partitioning: enabled (2g.10gb)
```

david (eng-runtime): eu-nonmig nodes run Driver 535.86.01 / CUDA 12.3 build; different minor versions. The rollout changed our kernel selection to prefer fast_matmul_v3 where available; fallback to matmul_v2_fallback occurs on older drivers. That maps to the warnings.

chen (eng-ml): that explains a plausible root cause: numerics/ordering difference in fallback kernel for MIG partitions + deterministic=false previously masked it. But we reproduced with deterministic flags and still see divergence — which suggests a real kernel-level difference causing decoding path changes.

raj (cust-succ): Acme is on a paid dedicated plan for EU. This is customer-impacting. They want either a rollback or a mitigation immediately.

maria (support): they requested rollback to previous model variant or pin to redwood-3b-v1.9 for EU traffic. Can we do a regional pin while we investigate?

david (eng-runtime): yes — we can add a routing rule to pin EU->redwood-3b-v1.9 within 10 minutes. That will stop new incorrect responses. We'll monitor backlog and cost.

chen (eng-ml): parallel path: we should reproduce locally with the exact driver/kernel combination. I'll spin up a repro container using Driver 530.41.03 and the fallback kernel to compare numerics. If confirmed, we either revert the kernel selector change for MIG partitions or add a software patch that normalizes attention accumulation.

olivia (sre): operational plan proposed:
- immediate: add routing rule to pin EU traffic for customers on affected plans to previous model (v1.9) or route to non-MIG nodes if available. (10m ETA)
- short-term: rollback kernel selector change for MIG partitions in next release job. (2–4 hours)
- long-term: add matrix tests that run inference across driver versions / MIG partitions during release canary. (scheduled)

maria (support): Acme responded: they can tolerate short pin but want timeline and root cause before EOD.

david (eng-runtime): routing rule applied: eu-region pin active (rule-id: rule-7721). Confirming new requests now go to redwood-3b-v1.9.

deploy-bot: routing rule rule-7721 activated by david at 2026-03-14T03:05:12Z

maria (support): I informed Acme and updated INC-7812 with mitigation. They ran tests and reported outputs aligned again. :thumbsup:

chen (eng-ml): initial local kernel repro shows small but consistent differences in GEMM accumulation ordering that cascade into token selection at decode step 14. I will open PR to force deterministic reductions in that path; if accepted, we can avoid rollback in future.

david (eng-runtime): for audit: linking to the rollout change CL: https://git.internal/redwood/rollouts/CL-9421 and kernel selector PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/PR-5012

olivia (sre): monitoring: setting alert for output-quality-sla for eu clusters to detect similar diffs automatically (inc threshold = 0.8 accuracy drop)

maria (support): moving INC-7812 to "mitigated" while root cause work continues. Thanks everyone.

acme-ops: thanks team — appreciate the quick pin. we'll keep running tests and will reopen if we see regressions.

maria (support): follow-ups: chen/david to produce ROE (root cause evidence) doc; olivia add driver/partition matrix to canary checklist; raj to confirm contract credits if any required.

(End of thread)
